## Description
Post-closure reliability defect in the Server-owned address reachability probe delivered under #43. The periodic sweep in `crates/nession-server/src/probe.rs::run_probe_sweep` awaits every TCP dial **serially**, with a five-second timeout per address, while `spawn_probe_task` schedules sweeps every 30 seconds. The documented #43 limit is 10 addresses per Agent, not a global limit. With two registered Agents each advertising ten nonresponsive addresses, a single sweep can consume approximately 100 seconds; subsequent interval ticks cannot restore the intended 30-second freshness. No new feature or new probe service is needed.

## Reproduction
**Static source proof, not yet an executed runtime benchmark:**
1. Register two Agents, each with ten valid but blackholed WebSocket endpoints.
2. `list_probe_targets()` returns both address sets. `run_probe_sweep` executes nested `for` loops and awaits `probe_once` on each; `probe_once` uses `timeout(PROBE_TIMEOUT=5s, TcpStream::connect(...))`.
3. In the worst case, 20 sequential timeouts consume ~100 seconds, excluding scheduling overhead. The next periodic sweep is therefore late even though `PROBE_INTERVAL=30s`.
4. Attach/Agent views may display old reachability/RTT while the Server remains responsive; actual impact on route selection requires runtime verification.

## Root Cause
The sweep has no bounded global/per-Agent concurrency. It snapshots all targets once and performs every dial sequentially; the periodic ticker cannot make progress while the sweep is still running. `AgentRegistry::update_address_status` also matches only Agent ID + URL, so a delayed result may be applied after a same-URL re-registration; that separate ABA concern is **hypothesis**, not included in the primary acceptance scope without proof.

## Impact
An ordinary multi-node deployment with several unreachable LAN/VPN addresses can make the Server's reachability information stale for minutes. This undermines #43's 30-second periodic status intent and Nession's work-continuity goal: network complexity should not surface as misleading connection state. It does not prove that an existing P2P socket disconnects.

## Fix Direction
Bound probe concurrency across the full sweep, preserve per-address timeout and avoid unbounded task spawning. Keep registry writes scoped to the currently registered address generation if a concurrent sweep makes replacement races possible. Do not change the Client's route selection, authentication, or Relay fallback contracts. Avoid an additional scheduler or background task per address.

## Location
- [Server probe loop](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/main/crates/nession-server/src/probe.rs)
- [Agent Registry target snapshot and result write](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/main/crates/nession-server/src/registry/agent.rs)
- Historical accepted multi-address design: #43 (remains closed; its SCs covered basic reachability and fallback, not multi-Agent sweep duration).

### Success Criteria
- [x] SC-01 In an isolated real Server/AgentRegistry fixture with at least two Agents × ten blackholed addresses and a short configurable test probe timeout, all 20 statuses settle within a bounded sweep deadline materially below the serial 20×timeout baseline; the fixture asserts the exact elapsed duration, probe counts and no unbounded task growth.
- [x] SC-02 Under concurrent re-registration of one Agent while probes are pending, stale results cannot overwrite a successor registration's address status; unchanged registrations still receive their matching results.

**SC scenario mapping:** SC-01 → SCN-06 (controlled latency/resource measurement; isolated runtime Case); SC-02 → SCN-03 (real asynchronous registry/probe lifecycle Case). Use a CI-supported isolated Rust runtime/protocol Case at exact PR SHA, deterministic local TCP listeners or controllable blackhole dial fixture, bounded runtime and cleanup; no external network or credentials required. SC-02 is included because parallelization would otherwise introduce a demonstrable registration race.
